thread:
anna: Quick follow-up on the API-key scoping RFC — proposing we move to a 2-tier model: org-scoped keys for org admin ops and project-scoped keys for apps/services. Service tokens should be ephemeral by default (minted via a token-exchange endpoint). Thoughts?

shiv: +1 on ephemeral for services. How do we handle existing long-lived keys used by infra jobs and CI?

kevin: We need a migration path. Suggestion: allow exchange of long-lived keys for short-lived bearer tokens (1h default) and emit a rotation webhook so infra can rotate without downtime.

lia: Concern: a lot of infra tools embed keys in Terraform vars and external systems. We should avoid breaking those flows abruptly. Compatibility window needed.

anna: Agreed. Proposal: implement an exchange endpoint that accepts old key and returns a wrapped ephemeral token. Also provide a "compat" mode that keeps the same effective scope but forces TTL and issues a rotation webhook for apps to catch up. Example header usage: 
```
Authorization: Bearer rwd-exchange-<id>
x-rwd-project: proj-123
```

tara: For RBAC mapping — do we keep owner/editor/viewer or move to permission-sets? I lean permsets for finer-grain controls.

shiv: Permsets + role-aliasing. During migration map legacy roles to a default permset. Allow admins to tune permsets per project/org.

kevin: One more: telemetry and auditing. All exchange events must include original principal, original key id, new token id, and the TTL in the audit log. This will make forensics possible if something goes wrong.

buildbot: deploy-bot: canary rollout scheduled for 2026-06-15 02:00 UTC for token-exchange endpoint (10% of traffic, eng-infra + eng-ml).

anna: Action items: 1) Add migration section to RFC with sample curl, compat flag, and rotation webhook example (I'll write). 2) Draft permset mapping table from legacy roles (kevin?). 3) Define audit events schema for exchange + rotation (I'll own). 4) SDK changes: add client.mint_service_token() and an opt-in compat flag (lia to coordinate docs).

kevin: I'll draft the mapping table and a short compatibility timeline. Target: EOD Friday for a PR on the RFC branch.

lia: I'll start an SDK PR stub and a short guide for Terraform/CI flows — include examples for both long-lived -> ephemeral exchange and webhook-driven rotation.

anna: Quick sample curl for RFC draft (putting here so it's searchable):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/token/exchange \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer OLD_LONG_LIVED_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project":"proj-123","compat":true}'
```

shiv: We also need to think about rate-limiting on the exchange endpoint to avoid noisy neighbors. Suggest per-key burst limits and a project-level throttle.

kevin: Good call. Add to RFC: per-key 60 req/min burstable, project-level 500 req/min. Can tune after canary.

tara: For service-to-service auth patterns, is the plan to recommend token-exchange via a local sidecar (short-lived tokens on node) or direct minting by the CI pipeline?

anna: Recommend sidecar for production (rotation + local caching) and CI can do exchange at build time with limited TTL. Document both patterns.

lia: One last note: update the Console so token metadata shows "origin: exchanged" and links to the audit event. Ops folks asked for that.

anna: Great — if no objections I'll fold these into the RFC tomorrow and open the migration PR. Thanks!

shiv: :thumbsup:

tara: :eyes: will review the RFC PR

kevin: ack, will send the mapping table later today

buildbot: deploy-bot: canary started (10% traffic)

anna: pinging @kevin for the mapping table link once ready.

kevin: posted draft mapping table in the RFC branch — link: https://git.redwood.ai/r/redwood/rfcs/+/token-scoping-mapping (edit mode).

anna: got it, thanks. I'll incorporate and send for review.
